brief: Trump-Xi summit: trade truce extended two months per Bessent; Xi pressed the US toward an "oppose" (not just "do not support") Taiwan-independence stance and floated AI-safety dialogue; GS sees nothing market-moving yet, awaiting the official readout, with Iran mediation the area to watch. Banxico held its rate at 6.50% unanimously, as GS and consensus expected, but GS views the 2026/27 inflation forecasts as too optimistic, with inflation risk skewed up and growth risk skewed down; GS's EM FX desk stays tactically short USDMXN (17.80 support, 18.00 psychological level) as fresh MXN shorts build. For Brazil's election, GS lays out nine cross-asset trades positioning for a Lula-Bolsonaro race that has narrowed to a near-binary, first-round-possible outcome. On AI capex, GS's baseline has 2027 hyperscaler spend beating consensus even as growth decelerates (100% to 54% to 12% through 2028), with capex now exceeding operating cash flow, forcing more debt/equity funding. On PMIs, GS argues September's multi-year-high flash prints overstate growth (nominal bias, ~2pt inflated) and that the resulting Treasury selloff was an overreaction, keeping its 2.2% 2026 GDP forecast.
